## Appearance

Marilla is a tall, thin, and gaunt woman with sharp angles and a lack of curves. Her dark hair, which shows gray streaks, is worn twisted up behind her in a hard little knot secured by two wire hairpins. Over time, her hair has grown grayer, though her once angular appearance features a noticeably softer face than in her youth, when she was considered a dark and homely child.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P44](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0044), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P15](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0015)_

## Personality

A woman of narrow experience, rigid conscience, and sober, middle-aged habits, she is known for her strict, sensible, and self-contained demeanor. Unsympathetic to unromantic ideas or poetry, she remains resolute and determined once her mind is made up. Driven by a sense of duty, she aims to drill [Anne](../character/anne.md) into a tranquil uniformity of disposition. Additionally, she possesses a notable skill for making three-year-old homemade currant wine, a craft for which she is celebrated in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea).

## History

Marilla Cuthbert grew up as a dark, homely child, remaining sensitive about her childhood looks for fifty years, and later inherited an amethyst brooch from her mother. As a young woman, she was already grown up when the new house at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) was built, and she once quarreled with John Blythe, refusing to forgive him. Decades later, Marilla and her brother [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) decided to adopt an orphan boy from [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia) to help on their farm, but were shocked when eleven-year-old [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) arrived by mistake instead. Though initially planning to return the girl to Mrs. [Spencer](../character/spencer.md), Marilla felt deep pity upon hearing Anne's tragic backstory and saved her from being taken in by the cruel Mrs. [Blewett](../character/blewett.md), ultimately agreeing to let her stay at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). Marilla took charge of Anne's upbringing, teaching her daily chores and bedtime prayers, and eventually defended her when Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/lynde.md) insulted the girl's appearance. Over the next few years, Marilla navigated Anne's various misadventures—including an accidental dynamic where [Anne](../character/anne.md) mistakenly served currant wine to [Diana Barry](../character/di.md)—while gradually developing a deep, maternal love for the imaginative girl. When [Anne](../character/anne.md) later met with misfortunes, such as accidentally dying her hair green or breaking her ankle, Marilla faithfully nursed her and realized how precious [Anne](../character/anne.md) had become to her. Marilla supported Anne's academic ambitions, permitting her to take advanced classes with Miss [Stacy](../character/stacy.md), and felt immense pride mixed with nostalgia when [Anne](../character/anne.md) tied for first place on the Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) examination and left for Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy). Following Matthew's sudden death from shock over a bank failure, Marilla learned from an oculist that her own failing sight would require her to give up reading and sewing, forcing her to consider selling [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables).

## Quotes

> "Well now, yes. It always kind of gives me a thrill to see them ugly white grubs that spade up in the cucumber beds. I hate the look of them."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised P58](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0058)

> "It’s five miles; and as you’re evidently bent on talking you might as well talk to some purpose by telling me what you know about yourself."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P8](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0008)

> "No, I don’t want any of your imaginings. Just you stick to bald facts. Begin at the beginning. Where were you born and how old are you?"
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P10](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0010)

> "We’re not talking about poetry, Anne—we are talking about saying your prayers. Don’t you know it’s a terrible wicked thing not to say your prayers every night? I’m afraid you are a very bad little girl."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VII. Anne Says Her Prayers P11](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0011)

> "Well, you’ll have to do without your thrill. I hadn’t any material to waste on puffed sleeves. I think they are ridiculous-looking things anyhow. I prefer the plain, sensible ones."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XI. Anne’s Impressions of Sunday-school P10](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0010)

## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla serves as a strict guardian and mentor to [Anne](../character/anne.md), taking on the responsibility of teaching her domestic duties like cooking, praying, and keeping her room tidy. Though Marilla initially planned to return [Anne](../character/anne.md) after a mix-up brought an orphan girl instead of a boy, listening to Anne's tragic childhood moved her to offer the child a home. Their relationship experiences friction over Anne's wild imagination and quick temper, but Marilla steadily develops a deep care and affection for her.

- Commands — guardian ordering her to her room  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P22](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0022)</sub>
- Mentor of — teaching her to cook  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XVI. Diana Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results P27](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0027)</sub>

### [Lynde](../character/lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/lynde--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla and Mrs. [Lynde](../character/lynde.md) are long-time neighbors and close acquaintances who offer each other support and comfort during times of trouble. Although Mrs. [Lynde](../character/lynde.md) often provides unsolicited opinions and criticism regarding household matters, Marilla continues to value her advice when navigating local community events and managing Anne's upbringing.

- Friend of — neighbors and close acquaintances who comfort and help each other in tragedy  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P38](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0038), [v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P5](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0005)</sub>

### [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--matthew-cuthbert.md)

Marilla and [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) are siblings who live and work together at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). While Marilla handles the domestic duties and takes a firmer, practical approach to managing their household, [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) provides a gentler influence. Despite their differing temperaments, they collaborate closely on major decisions, such as choosing to keep and raise [Anne](../character/anne.md) together.

- Sibling of — brother and sister living together at Green Gables  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P7](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0007), [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P0](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0000), [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P1](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0001), +7 more</sub>

### [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/lynde.md) is Marilla's outspoken neighbor and friend who frequently visits [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to share local gossip and offer candid advice. Although Mrs. Lynde's blunt criticisms—such as insulting Anne's appearance—can cause sudden conflict, Marilla relies on her experience and practical counsel when dealing with the challenges of raising a child.
